newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's ADI half year profit rises.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's ADI half year profit rises.

text.p: Australian-government owned arms maker and property developer ADI Ltd on Tuesday announced a profit of A$11.6 million before tax and abnormals for the six months to December 31
The profit compared with a A$9.1 million loss for the corresponding period of 1995 and ADI predicted the improved profitability would be maintained into the next half year.
ADI, which the government plans to sell, said in a statement it would pay a fully franked dividend of 2.52 cents per share or A$9.2 million.

Revenue for the half year rose by A$57.5 million to A$293.1 million, in part because of the ADI's purchase of the defence, aerospace and telecommunications operations of Stanilite Pacific Ltd in July, the company said.
"The company's improved profitability (is) expected to be maintained in the second half of the (fiscal) year," managing director Ken Harris said in the statement.

"Increasing production at the A$150 million Benalla munitions facility, which was officially opened last August, and profits emerging from the Stanilite acquisition (are) expected to especially contribute to higher operating profits in this half."

ADI, an agglomeration of the Defence Department's armaments plants and formerly called Australian Defence Industries, will be sold in the next year or so, Defence Minister Ian McLachlan said last month.
The company has become a property developer since it replaced several old plants with the new one at Benalla in Victoria.
British Aerospace Plc's Australian subsidiary responded to reports of the impending privatisation by saying it would be keen to participate in any consolidation of the Australian defence sector.
